summary: Wave 2.5 (Notifications, Messaging, Global Search, Unified Admin Platform) tested end-to-end. 22/22 backend pytest cases pass covering: notification auth guards + list/prefs shape, reaction/comment/follow/apply/rsvp dispatch to recipient (with self-action suppression verified), notification CRUD (read, unread flip, mark-all-read, delete) + preferences persistence, messaging (DM idempotency by participant set, send message → bumps conversation.updated_at + unread_by[recipient]++, list, marks read on fetch, dispatches 'message' notification), search (shape with all 7 by_type buckets + {type,id,title,url}, case-insensitive company match, /suggest only returns people+companies+hashtags), and admin platform (all 8 endpoints 401/403 without admin JWT, 403 with community cookie, 200 with admin JWT, PATCH /users/{id}/role persists). Frontend Playwright verified: anonymous / shows header-search-input and hides notifications-bell; typing 2 chars opens header-search-dropdown; authenticated flow (seeded community cookie) shows notifications-bell + notifications-unread-count badge with real notification, dropdown lists notification-item-{id}, /notificaciones page lists notification-row-{id} with notification-toggle-{id} + notification-delete-{id}, /mensajes loads messages-page with messages-conversations + messages-conv-{id}, click loads messages-list, messages-input + messages-send persists new message-{id}; admin at /admin/platform (pcs_admin_token) renders admin-platform-page + admin-tabs with 12 summary metrics (admin-metric-*), and all 7 tabs (users, companies, posts, jobs, events, reports, activity) render admin-tab-content-{tab} with admin-table-{tab} and admin-row-{tab}-{i}. /admin dashboard has admin-platform-link (href=/admin/platform) and admin-documents-link (href=/admin/documents).

minor.issue: Occasional 500 from DuplicateKeyError on the (post_id, session_id) unique index when the same session posts a view twice concurrently. The existing pre-check with find_one races the insert. Should be an upsert or catch DuplicateKeyError → return {counted:false}.

action_items: OPTIONAL: harden POST /api/feed/posts/{id}/view against DuplicateKeyError (wrap the insert in try/except pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError → return {counted: false}). Not blocking Wave 2.5 but observed in backend log.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/admin_platform_routes.py POST /reports/{report_id}/resolve — the update filter uses `{_id: report_id}` but post_reports documents don't include a synthetic string _id (they get an ObjectId by default) and none of the other admin routes select `_id`. Report resolve will silently no-op. Suggest changing the schema to also store an app-level `id` (e.g. `rep_...`) or match by the Mongo _id string explicitly. Current tests could not exercise this because /api/admin/reports responses don't expose _id.

routes/feed_routes.py:464-486 register_view has a race between find_one and insert_one on a unique index (post_id, session_id). Under real anon traffic the frontend already emits duplicates → 500s in log. Fix: try/except DuplicateKeyError or use update_one(..., upsert=True) with $setOnInsert.

routes/messaging_routes.py send_message — the update_one call splits into two branches based on whether unread_inc is empty. When empty (only sender is a `user` participant), the code uses only $set; that's fine. But when the conversation has no other user participants (e.g. self-DM edge case) unread_inc={} makes it fall into the else branch — safe, but consider a single dict-merge to avoid branching. Also the payload's sender_kind='company' path validates ownership only when sender_id is truthy; if a caller passes sender_kind='company' without sender_id, it silently downgrades to user. Explicit 400 recommended.

routes/search_routes.py — `_regex(q)` uses re.escape but never anchors; large collections will cause full-collection scans. Fine for MVP; add TEXT indexes or hand off to Atlas Search once corpora grow.
services/notifications.py dispatch swallows ALL exceptions silently (bare except → return None). Consider logger.warning at least; today a schema drift would erase notifications with no trace.
AdminPlatformPage: token key is `pcs_admin_token` in localStorage — worth documenting in test_credentials.md so future testing agents don't guess.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Wave 2.5 backend surface is fully covered by /app/backend/tests/test_wave25_core.py (self-contained, uses conftest.py fixtures mongo_db + admin_headers). Two tricky details: (1) job.apply notification uses subject_type='application' and subject_id=<application_id>, NOT the job_id — assert on kind only; (2) admin frontend reads token from localStorage['pcs_admin_token']. If retesting Wave 1/2 regressions, run pytest backend/tests/test_wave2_business.py + test_feed_categories.py in parallel — they were previously green in iteration_13.
